main_text.p: ventat; quo sejuncti, quamvis inviti, ad regem ducuntur, qui utrumque absolvit, Deo quasi monstrante, uti ajebat, innocentiam utriusque; quòd triduanâ illâ pugnâ neuter ab altero armis esset superatus. --

4. Quia omnes illæ actiones jure divino illicitæ, quæ aut odio, aut vindictæ cupidine incitante, aut desperatione, aut alio quo affectu inordinato peraguntur. Verùm tales sunt duellatorum actiones: ut etiam illicitæ censeri debeant. Cum enim alterum esse nocentem, alterum innocentem, aut utrumque nocentem, aut innocentem, necessum sit, quid aliud consequetur, quàm ut qui innocens est, super injuriâ ab adversario sibi illatâ, semet ulcisci velit; cùm tamen ultio soli Deo relinquenda: & qui nocens est', affectu pravo, imò diabolico abreptus, innocen-

page.notes: Catchword "tem" is the first word of the next page and sits at the right below the last line. The word "innocen-" is split at the line end with its printed hyphen. The "4." opens a new paragraph. The mark after "est" is printed as an apostrophe-like sign and is transcribed as "'". "ajebat" and "ducuntur" are read from a small scan and may need checking.
